editorial:
Imagine being a teenager who already survived a killer doll, only to be sent to a strict military school where you have to follow rules every single second. That is exactly where you find Andy Barclay in this sequel. The vibe is a bit different this time because the setting feels trapped and orderly, which makes it even scarier when a chaotic little monster like Chucky shows up. You get to see a grown-up Andy who is tired of people thinking he is crazy, but he knows the nightmare is coming back for him. It is a fun mix of a coming-of-age story and a slasher flick that keeps things moving quickly.

What really works here is the balance between the scary moments and the dark humor. Chucky is still funny and mean, and the action scenes in the school are surprisingly creative. While some of the effects look a bit dated, they still add a creepy charm to the experience. If you love 90s horror, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head during a big school event. Andy and his friends fight Chucky in a final battle. Chucky gets tricked and ends up getting blasted by a huge firework rocket. The explosion blows him to pieces, seemingly destroying him for good this time. Andy finally gets some peace and the people around him realize he was telling the truth about the doll all along, giving him a happy ending.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves campy horror and killer dolls.
